Commentary: Jasprit Bumrah to Daryl Mitchell, out Caught by Yashasvi Jaiswal!! Sharp catch at forward short-leg and Jaiswal is thrilled as Gill hugs him. Daryl Mitchell was batting well outside his crease and was walking at Jasprit Bumrah. He does the same to this good length nipbacker, on off and middle. The thick inside edge on the forward defence hits the thigh pad and lobs to Jaiswal who's quite deep at forward short-leg. Taken easily and then the celebrations begin. Bumrah comes back and gets a wicket. As simple as that. New Zealand in big trouble now. The bottom-hand came off after the inside edge is found. 18:32 Local Time, 05:32 GMT, 11:02 IST: Stumps, Day 1 - What a stunning recovery from New Zealand. Nicholls was NZ's best batter according to data at this venue and he came to the fore. India picked up 4 wickets in the morning session and then reduced New Zealand to 70/5. But this lad was so relaxed that he knew he had everything under full control. And in GP, he found the perfect partner who transferred the pressure back on the bowlers through a counterattack. They stole ones, twos and converted twos to threes. GP was lightning quick and Nicholls was matching him as well. India looked toothless in that second session. They just had no idea how to stop the runs. At one point, even dots were difficult to build. Prasidh was leaking, Kamboj wasn't great either and Akash couldn't separate the duo despite running in hard.

In Washi they found some control and only around 70 overs did they even think of packing the field to stem the flow. Prasidh came back for a good spell of short ball ploy. Nicholls mishit one and offered a simple catch to backward square leg only for Pant to needlessly attempt the catch and confuse DDP. Nicholls and GP ticked along and even survived those couple of overs with the new ball to put New Zealand in command. Nicholls continued his love affair with this ground - he's now scored 5 hundreds and 4 fifties in just 15 innings. He put on a great show in front of his family and GP is now on the verge of his own hundred, which he will be keen to complete tomorrow.

Henry Nicholls (1/3): [Where does that one rank for you?] Um, yeah, I don't know. It's obviously, it's still pretty fresh to be honest. But yeah, it was really nice. I guess the position we're in to have that partnership with Glenn and I guess for us to both be there at the end of the day is even more pleasing. [Walking out fourth ball of the day, what was going through your mind?] Yeah, I was sort of rushing a little bit to get ready to the top to be honest. But yeah, I mean obviously they bowled incredibly well and we know when we play here that that can be the challenge when you lose the toss and get put in. But I think all the guys worked really hard and it was just nice to have that partnership from the middle session right through the end of the day.

Nicholls (2/3): [Five of your 12 Test centuries have been scored here at the Basin Reserve. What is it that you like so much about the Basin?] Yeah, I'm not sure. I was having a bit of banter with the groundsman. He was saying it's his first time, first year here and he said that the first game, or the second game, I scored the first hundred here. So he said this morning, he said, oh, it'd be great if you could be the first. And I said, oh, before the toss, I said, oh yeah, maybe tomorrow or later on. But yeah, I mean it's, it's a special place to play. I think anyone who's a cricket fan or plays cricket loves playing at the Basin and that's certainly, for me, is a traditional ground and it's a lot of history here. So yeah, so to have that many here is pretty special.

Nicholls (3/3): [That is very special, very special because your family was here with you today. What does it mean to have them in the crowd when you do something as special as you did out here?] Yeah, it was really awesome. You know, even the non-strikers' end, I'm just looking up and seeing the kids playing up there. And yeah, it's my wife's birthday today as well, shout out to Lucy, she's the rock and it was pretty cool to have them. My mum and dad were there as well. So just, yeah, a really special day. [You and GP put together a pretty good fight back. What were you saying to each other out there?] Yeah, I mean his energy is infectious, the way he came out. I guess put a bit more pressure on them probably allowed me just to go about my work. And really enjoyed batting with him. A couple of guys who love running really hard and putting a bit of pressure on the Indian side that way. So, he batted fantastically and like I say for us to both be not out certainly a boost for the dressing room.

Did India overthink about the match ups? Gill stressed on picking hit the deck bowlers for this Test and also adding batting depth. These two factors must have played a massive role in the omission of Mo Siraj. But hey, Siraj with 43 wickets is the leading wicket-taker for India in this WTC cycle. What looked brilliant this morning for India, is now looking tough for the visitors as the hosts are set to post a healthy first innings total. And India will be up against the trio if Henry, Jamieson and Duffy with some grass on the pitch. We'll leave you with that thought for the day and be back nice and early for all the Day 2 action. Tomorrow. Good night!
